Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: NRA mobile payment app/e-service aims to automate non-tax revenue payments and improve collection/reconciliation; instant payment service launch communications also highlight paying taxes into NRA accounts, indicating revenue collection via digital rails.
revision_notes: Both original sources were fetched and read. The 2022 NRA article confirms a mobile payment app for non-tax revenue and plans for ITAS/ASYCUDA online payment; the 2025 Substack article confirms the Instant Payment Service enables instant tax payment into NRA accounts, though phrased prospectively rather than as an established fact. A fresher and more authoritative source was found: an NRA Commissioner General statement (December 2025) confirming that the Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS) now enables electronic filing and payment of taxes, including income tax and vehicle tax, via mobile money/wallet. This supports the existing Value Code of 3 (Yes); the evidence base is updated to the December 2025 statement. Flagged for human review as this is a top-of-scale (comprehensive/'Yes') score on a 0-3 scale.
revised_comments: The National Revenue Authority's Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS) enables electronic filing and payment of taxes, including income tax and vehicle tax, via mobile money and wallet payments, as confirmed by the Commissioner General in December 2025. The NRA additionally operates a dedicated mobile payment application, launched in 2022 as part of the AfDB-supported Enhancing Tax Compliance (ENTACO) project, to automate non-tax revenue payments across government ministries, departments and agencies. The Bank of Sierra Leone's Instant Payment Service, launched in 2025, further supports instant payments into NRA accounts. Taken together, most government revenue types are payable through digital channels.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: Bank of Sierra Leone is described as owning and managing the National Payment Switch, routing transactions for settlement at BSL, indicating direct operation rather than only regulation.
revision_notes: The switsalone URL cited in the original row no longer resolves to the article content (it now redirects to the general site homepage) and could not be verified; treated as a dead/stale link. The premiermedia-sl article (April 2023) was fetched and confirms the National Payment Switch is 'owned and managed by the Bank of Sierra Leone', routing all transactions to BSL for settlement. This is corroborated by the National Payment Systems Act 2022 and the Bank of Sierra Leone Act 2019 (s.43(5)), both fetched and read, which explicitly empower the Central Bank to 'organise, own, participate in or operate' payment and settlement systems, and by a World Bank project document confirming the switch's launch on 29 April 2023 under a World Bank-supported financial sector reform programme. Evidence supports the original score of 5 (Direct Operation). Flagged for human review as this is a top-of-scale score on a 0-5 scale.
revised_comments: The Bank of Sierra Leone owns and manages the National Payment Switch, which routes all interbank and mobile money transactions to the Bank for settlement. The National Payment Systems Act 2022 and the Bank of Sierra Leone Act 2019 explicitly empower the Central Bank to organise, own, participate in or operate payment and settlement systems, going beyond a purely regulatory role. The switch, part of a World Bank-supported financial sector reform programme, was launched on 29 April 2023, with the Bank of Sierra Leone directly operating the platform and settling transactions across banks, mobile money operators and fintechs.
